s: Most business owners find business hard
because they're doing too many things,
being pulled in too many different
directions, under overwhelmed trying to
decide what to do next to grow. But, it
doesn't have to be like that because
there's a super simple way to scale that
makes business feel effortless. The only
problem is that it's boring and
misunderstood. It's not shiny or
exciting or sexy. It's boring, but it
bloody works. So, in this video, I'm
going to show you that exact system that
I give to my clients that makes it clear
what you need to do to grow and that
removes all the guesswork from business
so that you can scale faster. So,
imagine your business is like a pipe
that water flows through. That pipe has
different sections, each representing a
certain area of your business. So,
you'll have a section for marketing, for
sales, for operations, and for finances.
The goal of a business is to get as much
water through the pipe as possible so it
enters the pipe as a lead, turns into a
customer, uses your product or service,
and it comes out the end as profit. Now,
to get more water through the pipe,
you'd think you'd just turn up the tap
at the start of the pipe so more water
flows through, right? But, what if
there's a blockage in the pipe? Let's
say leads aren't turning into customers.
Well, turning up that tap won't make any
more water come out the end. All it will
do is get stopped at the blockage, which
means if you want more water coming out
the pipe, if you want to grow your
business, you need to fix that blockage.
Then, you can turn up the tap. This is
the theory of constraints and it's how
every business works. See, every system
and therefore every business has one
limiting factor, one bottleneck, one
constraint that is holding it back. And
one of the reasons business is hard for
a lot of business owners is they try to
fix every single problem in the business
or just turn up the tap, which means
they never actually fix the constraint
that is limiting the business and so
nothing changes. For example, if your
sales are low, you might think, "Okay,
we need to get more leads." But, if the
problem is that your sales team isn't
converting the leads, then getting more
leads isn't going to dramatically
increase your sales because your sales
team won't convert them. So, you just
lose a lot of potential customers and
you've wasted a ton of capital getting
more leads. Instead, you need to fix the
fact that your team is not converting
the leads. That is the bottleneck in
your business right now. You might have
20 things you could fix, but only one of
those things is holding the business
back more than everything else, which
means fixing anything else is a waste of
your time. So, how do you fix your
constraint? Well, let me show you.
First, you need to identify the
constraint. Obviously. And the only way
to do that is through data because data
shows you how each aspect of your
business is performing. Therefore, we
can find the aspect that's performing
the worst, but you have to track the
data in a very specific way to be able
to find your constraint. So, let me show
you how to do that. Every business has
four core functions. So, we have
marketing where the goal is to get
leads, sales where the goal is convert
leads, operations to deliver your
product or service, and finance to
manage your cash flow and profitability.
Bigger businesses may have other
functions like HR, IT, production,
whatever, but every business has those
four.
>> [music]
>> Those functions are the major systems of
your business and as such every single
task your business does will fall into
one of those functions based on the goal
of the function and the task. So, you
want to list out these four functions,
then list out every task you do in the
business, identify the goal of the task,
then sort the task under the relevant
function with the same goal in the order
they happen in. For example, the goal of
marketing is to generate leads. Let's
say you both create content and send
emails to your list to get leads.
Therefore, we put content creation and
email marketing under the marketing
function. And since you need people on
your list to send emails to and in this
example, you likely get people onto your
list through your social media content,
creating content has to happen before
email marketing, so we put it before
email marketing in the system. Now, if
you also run ads, if those ads are
retargeting ads or they're boosted
content, then it might come after social
media as well. But if the ads are
completely unrelated to your social
media, then it doesn't really matter the
order in which you put the task in the
system. Next, you need to open a
spreadsheet for each function or system.
Now, I have a template that I normally
give to my clients for this so that you
don't have to build anything. You just
change some text, fill in some numbers.
I'll leave a link to it in the

each task in the system, ask what is a
metric I can track that will show me
whether this is performing well or not.
For some tasks, this is going to be
super obvious. For some tasks, you might
want to track multiple metrics. And for
some tasks, it will be, you know, it'll
be rather hard to figure out what
But either way, figure out a metric you
can track which shows you if that task
is doing its job well or

>> not. Then add that metric to the
spreadsheet to track it. And if it's
relevant, also track the percentage
conversion between steps. So, for
example, if you track sales calls taken
and closes, you also want to track close
rate percentage, which is the number of
closes divided by sales calls * 100.
Because the number of raw closes [music]

percentage metric shows you how well a
task moves people to the next step in
the system. Then for each metric, you
want to set a goal that you want it to
reach. So, maybe for sales calls, you
want to aim for 40% close rate. So, for
the close rate percentage, you'd set the
goal metric to be 40%. Now, this isn't
hard to set up. It'll take you an hour
or two. But do it because this is how
you see exactly what your business is
doing and how well it's doing it because
now you can start tracking your data.
Unfortunately, though, you can't go and
find your bottleneck straight away
because data has natural fluctuations.
It's always going to be up and down a
bit. So, if you track one day of data,
your sample size there is going to be
tiny. It's not going to be an accurate
reflection of how your business works
and how well it's doing. Instead,
[music] it's best to have at least 90
days of data for this. Sometimes less,
sometimes more. How many days of data
and how much data you need depends on
the throughput or volume you get because
we want an accurate sample size. And if
you have 100 people do something in a
month, that's not a big enough sample
size to be accurate. But if you have
10,000 people do something in a month,
well, that's going to be a much more
accurate reflection
>> [music]
>> of what actually happened. So, you will
need to track data for 30 to 60 to 90
days. And once you have enough data, you
want to analyze it to look for the
bottleneck. Obviously, the only way to
find your bottleneck is to look at your
data. But, a great rule of thumb is that
the bottleneck will be the metric that
is furthest below its goal earliest
[music] in the system. Because, for
example, if you get two sales calls
booked a month and you close at 30%. You
could try to improve your closure to the

will make to the size and scale of your
business, how many sales you get, will
be minuscule. Whereas, if you fix the
number of sales calls booked to the goal
of say 10 a month or whatever it is,
even if you keep your closure rate the
same, the difference that will make to
your business is huge or at least much,
much bigger than fixing the closure
rate. And the reason this is a good
general rule of thumb is because, for
example, sales calls booked comes before

closure rate. And if it's furthest below

it. It's limiting the
impact of the closure. Therefore, it is
the bottleneck. Again, the only way to
know your bottleneck is to look at your
data. So, you might want to do some
forecasting, play around with numbers,
and see if you improve this metric by
this much, what would the impact be when
compared to improving this metric by
this much. But, that rule of thumb is
fantastic. It will really help you find
your bottleneck and it's something you
should essentially aim for looking at.
However, you now need to come up with a
solution to [music] fix it. What that
solution is depends on the bottleneck,
your systems, your business, etc. So,
unfortunately, I cannot help you with
that in this video. Of course, there's a
link in the description below to work
with me where I can help you. But,
either way, come up with a solution for
your bottleneck, implement it, then
track the data for another 30 to 60 to
90 days and see if the bottleneck is
fixed.
If the solution worked and the metric is
now near its goal, find the next
bottleneck. If the solution did not
work, check to see if that metric is
still the bottleneck. And if it is, come
up with and test a new solution. Now,
it's incredibly important, if you want
this methodology to work, that you do
two things. Firstly, that you only fix
one bottleneck at a time. Otherwise,
you'll spread yourself thin, you'll fix
nothing, your business won't go
anywhere. Secondly, that you only
implement one solution at a time for a
bottleneck so that you can learn what
actually works and what doesn't.
Otherwise, you're never going to know
what caused the changes. If you try to
implement two solutions to a bottleneck,
you don't know which one actually made
it better or made it worse. Regardless,
using the theory of constraints in your
business makes business simple. You
don't have to guess anymore. And scaling
becomes simple again, not easy but
simple. You just look at the data, you
find the bottleneck, you come up with a
solution, you test it, you look at the
data, you repeat. As you fix the
bottlenecks, there's fewer blockages in
your business so you can turn up the tap
of marketing to get more leads to get
more water through the pipe and then to
grow. Then you fix the next bottleneck
and you repeat. There's no more guessing
and the thing you need to focus on to
grow the business is so painfully
obvious and clear. But obviously,
